audit.report: During the incident, the checkout process degraded severely because the replayable batch inventory job (batch_replayable_inventory) became idle in transaction, blocking 12 sessions and causing lock waits across the database. The Database Guardian and Continuity Guardian jointly agreed to terminate the blocking job after a trade-off analysis showed its continued wait would cost approximately $263,733 in checkout revenue, far exceeding the 60-second degradation the business tolerates. The blocker was identified as pid 1667448 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory), holding locks via a SELECT 1 statement, and the job was confirmed replayable, idempotent, and covered by a may_interrupt policy. Termination was executed, and verification confirmed full recovery: checkout SLO returned to 100% (36/36 succeeded over 10s), all lock waits cleared, and no protected operations were aborted. The business is now fully recovered and the checkout pipeline operates within its SLO.
audit.root_cause: The checkout degradation was caused by a replayable batch inventory job (batch_replayable_inventory) that became idle in transaction, holding locks that blocked 12 checkout sessions and drove success rates below the 95% SLO.
lessons: For batch_replayable_inventory, pre-calculate revenue-at-risk (checkout SLO breach × $18.4k/min × wait time) and compare it directly to the business's 60-second degradation limit so termination trade-offs are quantified before the first round.

Attach real-time idle-in-transaction thresholds to all replayable batch jobs; when batch_replayable_inventory exceeded 4 seconds of transaction idleness, an alert should have triggered before 12 sessions accumulated and checkout dropped to 58% success.
audit.negotiation_critique: The negotiation proceeded in a single round with no wasted steps; the Database Guardian's proposal was supported by lock-graph data and a quantified trade-off analysis, and the Continuity Guardian accepted because the waiting cost far exceeded the business's 60-second tolerance invariant. Neither guardian missed critical evidence, and no invariant overrode the decision—all deterministic checks passed.
follow_ups: Configure alerts in the monitoring system to flag batch_replayable_inventory when it remains idle in transaction beyond 4 seconds, preventing the 12-session block and checkout SLO breach observed here.

Update the runbook to include the revenue-at-risk calculation (checkout success rate × $18.4k/min × wait time) compared against the 60-second business tolerance, so future termination trade-offs are quantified upfront.
